source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: For LIPUS stimulation, we used a transducer (A314S; 1 MHz, 0.75 in.; Olympus, Waltham, MA, USA) that received an ultrasound signal from a function generator (AFG 3022B; Tektronix, Irving, TX, USA) and a radiofrequency amplifier (25A250A; Amplifier Research, Souderton, PA, USA). The acoustic parameters of the transducer were measured using a hydrophone needle (SN2392; Precision Acoustics, Dorchester, Dorset, UK) inserted into the midpoint in front of the transducer surface with the sensitivity calibration data about 46 mV/MPa. The needle position was adjusted using the XYZ dynamic axis to locate the position relative to the maximum hydrophone signal. NSC-34 cells were subjected to LIPUS stimulation at a center frequency of 1.15 MHz, with a FWHM of 17.5 mm, a focal length of 80 mm, a spatial peak average temporal average intensity of 356.78 mW/cm<sup>2</sup>, and a pulse repetition frequency of 1 kHz for 8 min through a water-containing acrylic tube.

flags.reason: Paper reports statistics as 'at least three independent measurements' but does not state the number of independent cell cultures/dishes exposed to LIPUS.

Hydrophone measurement was made in water in front of the transducer; cells were exposed via a water-filled tube through a thin culture medium layer with no skull or tissue path, so the free_field vs in_situ distinction is not explicitly stated by the paper.
Paper does not state duty cycle or pulse duration for this LIPUS protocol, only PRF (1 kHz) and total duration (8 min).
NSC-34 is an immortalized motor-neuron-like hybrid cell line, not primary cultured neurons; closest vocabulary match (cultured_neurons) is imperfect.

species: mouse (NSC-34 motor neuron-like hybrid cell line)
readout_other: Western blotting (GRP78, ATF-6, CHOP, caspase-12, BAX, BCL-2, phospho-AKT, NFAT, phospho-NF-κB); immunofluorescence (CHOP); DCFH-DA reactive oxygen species assay; TMRM mitochondrial membrane potential staining; Fluo-4/AM real-time calcium imaging; live-dead cell viability staining
direction_notes: LIPUS did not directly assess neuronal excitability; it reduced ER stress and oxidative stress markers, increased BCL-2/BAX ratio, activated Ca2+ signalling, NFAT, NF-κB and AKT, and improved motor neuron survival under thapsigargin/H2O2/tunicamycin challenge.

exposures.label: LIPUS stimulation of NSC-34 motor neuron-like cells

target.label: NSC-34 motor neuron-like hybrid cell line (motor neuron/spinal cord-derived)

timing.protocol_description: NSC-34 cells were subjected to LIPUS stimulation at a center frequency of 1.15 MHz, with a FWHM of 17.5 mm, a focal length of 80 mm, a spatial peak average temporal average intensity of 356.78 mW/cm2, and a pulse repetition frequency of 1 kHz for 8 min through a water-containing acrylic tube. Cells were stimulated on days 1 and 3, with cytotoxic challenge (thapsigargin, H2O2, or tunicamycin) applied for 6 h on day 3.
